speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari
text: asked the Minister for Education (a) whether there are plans to review the current practice of ranking teachers for performance appraisal every year as an approach to cultivate a high performance workforce and identify low performers; (b) whether the benefits of performance ranking outweighs its challenges, especially in terms having to ensure a "correct" distribution of scores and creating a culture of individual competitiveness that is detrimental to team work and team dynamics; and (c) what alternatives has the Ministry considered for staff performance appraisals other than the current method.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Ministers for Education)
text: It recognises individuals who do well in fulfilling the missions and objectives of the organisations.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Ministers for Education)
text: This way, stronger performing officers are identified and recognised, while weaker ones are provided developmental opportunities to improve.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Ministers for Education)
text: In addition, it also helps to moderate differences in the supervisors' assessments and establish common standards of performance.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Ministers for Education)
text: Besides their individual performances, teachers are assessed holistically across many different areas, like how they work and collaborate with others and contribute to the learning of their peers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Ministers for Education)
text: In addition, teachers are also expected to be able to deliver effective teaching and pastoral care, support students in their character development and interact well with them.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Ministers for Education)
text: The Ministry of Education (MOE) seeks to develop a culture of professionalism and a strong sense of mission in our teachers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Ministers for Education)
text: The appraisal system is but one of the many tools used to achieve this.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Ministers for Education)
text: We encourage teachers to pursue various professional development opportunities, from formal programmes to informal support through networked learning communities and mentoring arrangements.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Ministers for Education)
text: To spur teamwork, our schools give out Outstanding Contribution Awards every year in recognition of school staff who collaborate successfully to make outstanding contributions to the school community.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Ministers for Education)
text: The President's Award for Teachers brings out excellence in teaching and is the highest honour bestowed on teachers for professionalism.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Ministers for Education)
text: We will continue to develop and improve our teachers' skills and expertise to deliver a student-centric and value-driven education and, in so doing, enhance our students' learning and growth.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Jack Welch started forced ranking in his company, General Electric, and it would be good to know that General Electric has done away with forced ranking.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Given the debate on the merit of performance ranking, would MOE consider doing away with forced ranking and, instead, raise education officers' salaries to ensure their substantive grades commensurate with their official appointments and also adopt a criteria-based appraisal for performance?

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I want to thank the Member Mr Zainal Sapari for his passionate plea and also his supplementary questions.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Allow me to reassure him that MOE will continue to finetune our appraisal system with the focus on supporting the development opportunities and potential of our teachers.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: While there are debates about the pros and cons of ranking, I think it has proven that ranking imposes objectivity, fairness, rigour and discipline in the appraisal system.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: It also differentiates officers' performance relative to their peers and helps to establish common standards of performance amongst supervisors.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: And I just want to give an example.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: One, appraisal, as in any form of assessment, should be both formative and summative.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: At the moment, our appraisal system is quite summative.

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Are there plans to get teachers to have teacher mentors or buddies so that a more formative approach to their appraisal can be done throughout the year before the final assessment for performance bonus or promotion?

speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The second supplementary question is this: would the Ministry consider also getting feedback from students as well as parents on how teachers perform rather than just based on peer assessment among teachers and their reporting supervisors?

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I want to thank Dr Intan Mokhtar for her supplementary questions.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I want to assure her that the annual appraisal is not a static one.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: In fact, the development of our teachers, 30,000 of them, is really key to achieving our goals in education for our students' development.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: In order to help our 30,000-plus educators improve their skills, we, indeed, use several avenues for our educators to receive feedback.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: In so doing, we seek to help our teachers and supervisors learn to give one another feedback and also learn to receive feedback in a very constructive manner through daily interactions and not only at the point of appraisal.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: A lot of the Members in the House are parents and we have different apps, whether it is ClassDojo, Snapp and so on, for us to give inputs and feedback to teachers and also to the school leaders.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: So, actually that avenue is open to the parents as well.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: One, as my colleague Mr Zainal Sapari has mentioned that a lot of progressive companies have actually done away with such performance evaluation systems.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Two, we know the consequences of forced ranking.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: There are some negative aspects of forced ranking in that there are instances when employees get pushed up in terms of their ranking because of very vocal supervisors who are able to speak up for them at ranking sessions.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: And then there are some jobs where some staff who are actually more visible due to the nature of their work and the way some of them carry out their work.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I also want to ask the Senior Parliamentary Secretary to consider asking the Minister of Education and the Ministry if they could do away with such award schemes like the Outstanding Teacher Award.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Because out of the many thousands of educators, there are many who actually do very well.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: And it is really quite difficult to finalise a list of educators who should be honoured.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: In fact, to run a race whereby only a few win the trophy might be a race that, I think, the Minister has been asking for us not to run.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: We should run races where as many as possible can make it to the finish line, and as many as possible can meet a good or great performance standard.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I want to thank our Government Parliamentary Committee Chair Ms Denise Phua for her supplementary questions and also her suggestions.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I want to assure all the Members that MOE continues to look at the performance appraisal systems that are practised by other organisations.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: And we do know that each appraisal system comes with the pros and cons.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: In relation to the original Parliamentary Question, the question is whether we can do away with ranking and do an assessment based on the job type.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: We certainly want to do so in a manner that is fair and just and that recognises efforts of our passionate teachers.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: So, just allow me to explain why, currently, this appraisal system is deemed as a fair assessment.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: For example, if it is simply ranked by job function, job scope.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: And a newly appointed principal who has been promoted upwards from a vice principal to a principal based on job scope but not yet moved up in substantive grade.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: If he or she is then compared, in terms of performance, to the rest of the principals, and some of whom will be very senior principals in higher grades, actually, in so doing, the showing for the newly appointed principal may well pale in comparison with the senior principals.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: At the same time, we also want to make sure there are also avenues for us to express gratitude and recognise the efforts of our teachers.
